questions.question:
Select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of idioms/phrases.

To take the bull by the horns

options.text: To deal with a dangerous prisoner
To deal with a hopeless student
To deal with an annoying person
To deal with a difficult situation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **To deal with a difficult situation**.

__
 
• The phrase **"To take the bull by the horns"** means to confront a problem or a difficult situation directly and with courage. (किसी कठिन परिस्थिति का साहसपूर्वक सामना करना)

 
 
• **Example:** She decided to take the bull by the horns and confront her boss about the unfair workload.
 

 
• The correct meaning of this idiom reflects the idea of addressing a challenge head-on without hesitation. (सीधे और साहसपूर्वक चुनौती का सामना करना)

 
 
• **Example:** Instead of avoiding his financial issues, he took the bull by the horns and started budgeting carefully.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **To deal with a difficult situation**.

• **Example:** The police officer was trained to deal with dangerous prisoners, but this is not related to "taking the bull by the horns."
 
 

 
• **Option 2: To deal with a hopeless student** (एक निराशाजनक छात्र से निपटना) - This option also does not capture the essence of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher tried to motivate the hopeless student, but this situation doesn't align with the idiom's meaning.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: To deal with an annoying person** (एक परेशान करने वाले व्यक्ति से निपटना) - This option is incorrect as the idiom refers to facing a challenging situation, not a specific person.

questions.question:
Identify the grammatical mistake in a given sentence.

The psychological actions / of his wife / was thoroughly upset Mr. Amith / No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is two-fold: it involves **Subject-Verb Agreement** and **Voice/Tense construction**.
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**The psychological actions**," which is a plural noun phrase. Therefore, the singular auxiliary verb "**was**" is incorrect; it should be plural.
 
• Furthermore, the construction "**was thoroughly upset Mr. Amith**" is grammatically nonsensical. "Upset" here acts as the main verb. If the actions are the cause, the sentence should be in the active voice: "**upset Mr. Amith**" or "**have thoroughly upset Mr. Amith**."
 
• If the intention was to use the past tense, the correct plural form would be "**thoroughly upset Mr. Amith**" (without "was").
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The psychological actions of his wife **thoroughly upset** Mr. Amith."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The psychological actions"** – This is a correct plural subject phrase.
 
• **Option 3: "of his wife"** – This is a correct prepositional phrase identifying the source of the actions.
 
• **Option 2: "No error"** – This is incorrect because the verb phrase in Option 4 is fundamentally broken in terms of both number and structure.
 
• **Confusing 'Upset':** Note that "upset" can be an adjective (He is upset), a noun (a major upset), or a verb (The news upset him). In this sentence, it is used as a verb.

Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Seema said to Meera, "Why didn't you inform your father about the problem you were facing in the hostel?"

options.text: Seema asked Meera why she had not informed her father about the problem she had been facing in the hostel.
Seema told Meera why she had not informed her father about the problem she had been facing in the hostel.
Seema asked Meera why she had not informed her father about the problem she was facing in the hostel.
Seema asked Meera why she did not inform her father about the problem she was facing in the hostel.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** When converting a direct question into indirect speech, the question format is changed into a statement format, and the tense changes appropriately.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Why didn’t you inform" becomes "why she had not informed":**
 
 
• The past tense "didn’t inform" is changed to the past perfect "had not informed" to fit the rules of indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun "you" is changed to "she" to align with the perspective of the speaker.
 
 
 
• **"the problem you were facing" becomes "the problem she had been facing":**
 
 
• The past continuous tense "were facing" is changed to the past perfect continuous "had been facing" in indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun "you" is replaced with "she" to match the subject in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb "said to" becomes "asked":**
 
 
• Since the direct speech is a question, the reporting verb "said to" is changed to "asked" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed, and the sentence is presented in a declarative format.
 
• No question mark is used in the indirect statement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Seema asked Meera why she had not informed her father about the problem she had been facing in the hostel.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Seema told Meera why she had not informed her father about the problem she had been facing in the hostel." 
 
 
• Incorrect because the reporting verb "told" is used instead of "asked," which changes the context of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Seema asked Meera why she had not informed her father about the problem she was facing in the hostel." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "was facing" should be in the past perfect continuous tense ("had been facing") in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Seema asked Meera why she did not inform her father about the problem she was facing in the hostel." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "did not inform" does not follow the tense rules for indirect speech and should be changed to "had not informed."

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is written in the active voice?

options.text: Sleep disturbances are often caused by excessive mobile use.
Real-life conversations are being replaced by virtual interactions.
Experts suggest setting boundaries for mobile use.
Notifications are checked constantly by people of all ages.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To answer this question, let's break down each sentence to identify the voice (active or passive) used in each:**

__
 
• **1. Sleep disturbances are often caused by excessive mobile use.**

 
 
• This sentence focuses on the recipient of the action (sleep disturbances).
 
• This sentence is in the passive voice__ because it uses the auxiliary verb "are" + the past participle "caused," and the doer (mobile use) follows the word "by."
 
 
 
• **2. Real-life conversations are being replaced by virtual interactions.**
 __
 
• This sentence focuses on what is happening to the conversations.
 
• This sentence is in the passive voice__. It uses the continuous passive form "are being replaced."
 
 
 
• **3. Experts suggest setting boundaries for mobile use.**
 __
 
• This sentence focuses on the doer (Experts) performing the action (suggest).
 
• This sentence is in the active voice__. The subject "Experts" is performing the action directly, and there is no "be" verb combined with a past participle to indicate passivity.
 
 
 
• **4. Notifications are checked constantly by people of all ages.**
 __
 
• This sentence focuses on the object being acted upon (Notifications).
 
• This sentence is in the passive voice__. It follows the structure: Object + "are" + past participle "checked" + "by" + Subject.
 
 
 
• __So, out of the given sentences, options 1, 2, and 4 are written in the passive voice, while option 3 is written in the active voice__.
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: What is the term used to describe how the brain interprets the frequency of an emitted sound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pitch**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Pitch** is the perceptual property of sound that allows the brain to interpret the **frequency** of an emitted sound. 
• It is closely related to the **frequency of vibration**. Higher frequencies are perceived as higher pitch, while lower frequencies are perceived as lower pitch. 
• Pitch is a **subjective sensation**, meaning it is how humans perceive sounds rather than an objective, measurable property of the sound wave itself. 
• For example, a musical note produced by a tuning fork vibrating at **440 Hz** is perceived as the pitch "A" in musical terms. 
• This term is distinct from related terms like **tone** (refers to sound quality), **frequency** (a measurable property of sound waves), and **wavelength** (the spatial property of sound waves). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Frequency**: 
• It is the number of sound wave cycles that occur in one second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. 
• Humans generally hear frequencies ranging from **20 Hz** to **20,000 Hz**. 
• Frequency is an objective, measurable property of sound waves. 
• **Tone**: 
• It refers to the quality or character of sound, often determined by the sound's frequency and amplitude. 
• Musical tones, for instance, are characterized by a specific pitch, timbre, and duration. 
• **Wavelength**: 
• It is the physical distance between two consecutive peaks or troughs of a sound wave. 
• Wavelength is inversely proportional to frequency: higher frequency means shorter wavelength. 
• It is typically measured in meters (m). 
• **Applications of Pitch**: 
• In **music**, pitch helps differentiate musical notes and create harmony. 
• In **speech**, pitch variations convey emotions, questions, and emphasis. 
• It is also used in **sonar technology** and tuning musical instruments. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Distinction Between Related Terms:** 
• **Pitch**: A perceptual property that depends on frequency. 
• **Frequency**: A measurable property of the number of sound wave cycles per second. 
• **Wavelength**: The spatial distance between cycles of sound waves. 
• **Tone**: Refers to the quality or richness of sound. 
• **Biological Basis of Pitch Perception:** 
• The human ear perceives pitch via hair cells in the cochlea of the inner ear. 
• Specific regions of the cochlea are sensitive to different frequencies, a property known as **tonotopic organization**. </ul

questions.question: As per the Industrial policy resolution 1956 of India, industries were divided into how many category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** was a landmark policy document that shaped India's industrial development post-independence.
 
• As per this policy, industries were classified into **three categories**, depending on the degree of state control and participation:
 
 
• **Category A:** Industries exclusively under the state’s domain, such as defense, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• **Category B:** Industries where private enterprises could operate, but the state would progressively participate, such as chemicals, fertilizers, and road transport.
 
• **Category C:** All other industries that were left to private enterprise but still subject to state regulations and policies.
 
 
 
• The classification aimed to ensure a **mixed economy model** where both public and private sectors contributed to national development.
 
• It emphasized **state-led industrialization**, focusing on heavy industries and infrastructure to reduce dependency on foreign imports.
 
• This resolution was influenced by the **Soviet model of economic planning** and marked a significant step in implementing the vision of a socialist pattern of society in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• To promote a **socialist pattern of society** by reducing income inequalities and wealth concentration.
 
• To achieve a **self-reliant economy** by focusing on heavy industries and infrastructure development.
 
• To support the growth of **small-scale industries** for employment generation and equitable distribution of resources.
 
• To ensure the **balanced regional development** by setting up industries in less developed areas.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956:**
 
 
• It laid the foundation for the **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** in India.
 
• The focus on heavy industries led to the establishment of **steel plants, power projects, and machine-building industries**.
 
• It facilitated the **growth of the mixed economy**, combining public and private sector roles in industrial development.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 was implemented during the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)**, which emphasized heavy industries and a state-led development approach.
 
• The plan was designed by the renowned economist **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948:**
 
 
• The **1948 resolution** was more general and aimed at promoting industrial growth post-independence.
 
• The **1956 resolution** was more specific and focused on achieving a **socialist economy** by clearly defining the role of state and private sectors in industrialization.

• The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 identified **17 industries exclusively reserved for the state** under Category A.
 
• Category B included industries where both public and private sectors could coexist, with a focus on eventual state control.
 
• It played a significant role in promoting **import substitution** to reduce dependency on foreign goods.
 
• The resolution is considered a cornerstone of India's **economic and industrial policies** in the post-independence era.

• Countries with better opportunities and higher-quality education attract Indian talent, leading to a continuous brain drain.

questions.question: In the context of economy, which of the following is an example of Intermediate good?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper used for making utensils**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Intermediate goods** are goods that are used as inputs in the production of other goods and services. They are not the final products consumed by end users. 
• **Copper used for making utensils** is considered an intermediate good because it is used as a raw material in the production process to create finished goods such as utensils. 
• Unlike final goods, intermediate goods are not directly purchased for consumption; they undergo further processing or transformation in industries. 
• Examples of intermediate goods include **steel** used for manufacturing cars, **flour** used for baking bread, and **wood** used in furniture production. 
• Other options such as a **shirt**, **television purchased by households**, and **refrigerators** are considered final goods because they are consumed directly by individuals and are not used as inputs for further production. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Final Goods vs Intermediate Goods:** 
• Final goods are products consumed directly by households or businesses, providing utility without further processing. Examples include **appliances, clothing, and food items**. 
• Intermediate goods, in contrast, are used in the production process to create final goods. They are not consumed directly and include items such as **raw materials**, **components**, and **semi-finished products**. 
• **Characteristics of Intermediate Goods:** 
• They are used as **inputs** in the production process. 
• They are not intended for final consumption. 
• Examples include **chemicals** for manufacturing, **glass** for windows, and **copper** for utensils. 
• **Role in the Economy:** 
• Intermediate goods are crucial for industries as they form the backbone of the production process. 
• Their demand is a key indicator of industrial activity and economic growth. 
• For instance, increased demand for **steel** suggests growth in construction and automobile industries. 
• **Examples of Intermediate Goods:** 
• **Textile fabric:** Used in the production of clothing. 
• **Plastic:** Used in the manufacturing of toys, electronics, and containers. 
• **Wood:** Used in furniture production. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Economic Impact:** 
• Intermediate goods are often traded internationally, influencing global trade dynamics. For example, **India exports steel** to other countries for industrial use. 
• They contribute significantly to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** as their production is included in the calculation of industrial output. 
• **Distinction in Accounting:** 
• Intermediate goods are excluded from the calculation of GDP to avoid **double counting**, as their value is already embedded in the final goods. 
• **Government Policies:** 
• Government often imposes taxes or provides subsidies on intermediate goods to regulate industrial production and costs. 
• For example, reducing import duties on **raw materials** can promote domestic manufacturing industries. </ul

questions.question: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters through which of the following chamber of the heart of humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right atrium**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• Deoxygenated blood from various parts of the body returns to the heart through two large veins - the **superior vena cava** and the **inferior vena cava**. 
• The superior vena cava collects blood from the upper part of the body (head, neck, arms), while the inferior vena cava collects blood from the lower part of the body (abdomen, legs). 
• Both these veins empty deoxygenated blood into the **right atrium**, which is the first chamber of the heart to receive this blood. 
• From the right atrium, the blood is pushed into the **right ventricle** during atrial contraction. 
• The right atrium plays a crucial role in the circulation of blood as it acts as a receiving chamber for deoxygenated blood, initiating the pulmonary circulation process to re-oxygenate the blood. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Heart Chambers and Their Functions:** 
• The human heart has **four chambers**: the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle. 
• The **right atrium** receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it into the right ventricle. 
• The **right ventricle** pumps the blood to the lungs for oxygenation through the pulmonary artery. 
• The **left atrium** receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and sends it to the left ventricle. 
• The **left ventricle** pumps the oxygenated blood to the entire body through the aorta. 
• **Pulmonary Circulation:** 
• Deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs through the **pulmonary artery**. 
• In the lungs, carbon dioxide is exchanged for oxygen in the alveoli (tiny air sacs). 
• The oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium of the heart via the **pulmonary veins**. 
• **Systemic Circulation:** 
• Oxygenated blood is pumped from the left ventricle to the entire body through the **aorta**. 
• The body tissues utilize oxygen and nutrients from the blood, and in return, the blood picks up carbon dioxide and waste products. 
• Deoxygenated blood is then returned to the right atrium through the superior and inferior vena cavae. 
• **Valves of the Heart:** 
• The heart has four major valves to ensure the unidirectional flow of blood: **tricuspid valve, pulmonary valve, mitral valve, and aortic valve**. 
• The **tricuspid valve** is located between the right atrium and right ventricle, preventing backflow of blood. 
• The **pulmonary valve** lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery, regulating blood flow to the lungs. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **right atrium** is part of the systemic circulation and acts as the entry point for blood returning from the body. 
• The separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the heart's chambers is critical for efficient circulation in humans and other mammals. 
• The heart beats approximately **72 times per minute** on average, ensuring continuous circulation of blood. 
• Any obstruction in the flow of blood to or from the right atrium can lead to serious cardiovascular conditions, such as **right heart failure**. </ul

• During his time in India, Xuanzang visited major Buddhist sites such as **Nalanda University, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, and Kushinagar**. He studied at Nalanda, one of the most prestigious learning centers of the time. 
• Xuanzang documented his journey in the text titled **"Great Tang Records on the Western Regions" (Da Tang Xi Yu Ji)**, which provides invaluable insights into the political, social, and religious conditions of 7th-century India.
